newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end limit up on crop concerns.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end limit up on crop concerns.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled up their daily limit across the board, buoyed by fears that last weekend's freeze will slash yields to Florida's orange crop, market sources said.
The trade was noted as an aggressive buyer while the funds covered short positions throughout the day, dealers said.
The spot March contract closed up the 10.00-cent limit at 93.50 cents a lb, traded 93.50 to 85.10 cents. The back months up their 5.00-cent limit.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 7,000 lots.
There has been no official damage tally from the freeze and market talk varies. Some sources put crop losses at 20 percent while others insist damage will be minimal.
Besides, the freeze is not likely to put a dent in a record crop estimated at 220 million 90-lb boxes before the freeze, amid weak demand, some analysts said.

But concern led to trade buying and speculative short covering which fueled prices sharply higher. Forecasts of another cold front expected to hit the citrus belt this weekend brought in speculative demand, lifting prices the daily limit across the board.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said temperatures are not expected to fall low enough to harm fruit, however.
"It will be cooler this weekend across the entire state, but there is no major threat at this point," Davis said.
He said lows on Saturday are likely to range from 36 to 46 degrees Fahrenheit. "Obviously, these temperatures would not cause a problem for the citrus," he said.
Technically, the market was oversold and today's move nudged the fund shorts out of the market, PaineWebber's Bernard Savaiko said.
